questions.question: Thola Workwear: direct materials R480 000, direct labour R360 000, factory overheads R300 000, work-in-progress R30 000 at both the start and end of the year, twelve thousand units finished. Build the production cost statement levels aloud and give the unit cost, then state where the R240 000 selling commission and R60 000 office salaries belong.
questions.expected_answer: Prime cost: 480 000 plus 360 000 is R840 000. Add factory overheads of R300 000 for a total cost of production of R1 140 000. Add opening work-in-progress of R30 000 and subtract closing work-in-progress of R30 000 — the adjustment cancels — giving cost of production of finished goods of R1 140 000. Unit cost: 1 140 000 over twelve thousand is R95. The commission is a selling and distribution cost and the office salaries are administration; both live in the income statement and never enter the production cost statement, because a misfiled cost corrupts prime cost, total cost and unit cost at once.

questions.question: Using selling price R135, variable costs R90 per unit and fixed costs R360 000, calculate the break-even point, prove the R180 000 profit at twelve thousand units two ways, and explain what happens to break-even if the selling price rises while costs stay unchanged.
questions.expected_answer: Contribution: 135 minus 90 is R45. Break-even: 360 000 over 45 is eight thousand units. Proof one: four thousand units beyond break-even times R45 is R180 000. Proof two: sales of twelve thousand at R135 are R1 620 000, less variable costs of R1 080 000 and fixed costs of R360 000, leaves R180 000 — the two roads agree. A higher selling price widens the contribution per unit, so the same R360 000 of fixed costs is covered by fewer units and the break-even point falls; the safety margin between production and break-even widens, which is the interpretive sentence the marks want.

questions.question: A supplier's statement shows R52 400 against our ledger balance of R44 000. Our payment of R4 000 on the 30th is missing from the statement, the statement carries a R9 200 invoice for goods arriving only next month, and our ledger posted one invoice twice at R4 800. Reconcile both sides and state the general rule, then compute VAT owed from output R69 000, input R48 000, drawings of R8 000 excluding VAT and a bad debt of R4 600 inclusive.
questions.expected_answer: Statement side: 52 400 minus the 4 000 payment in transit minus the 9 200 invoice for undelivered goods gives R39 200. Ledger side: 44 000 minus the 4 800 duplicate gives R39 200 — agreement. Rule: timing differences sit on the statement side until the post catches up, and each side corrects only its own errors. VAT: 69 000 minus 48 000 is R21 000; drawings return the input claim, adding fifteen percent of 8 000, R1 200; the bad debt reclaims output of fifteen over one hundred and fifteen of 4 600, R600, subtracted. Amount owed to SARS: R21 600, money held in trust and never the business's own.
